deductions.name: Surface complexity weakens the scene's material and attention hierarchy
deductions.location: Foreground moth face, wings and spectacles; bench planks and knitted throw; central path; left tree and workshop canopy/table
deductions.finding: 11 carries much more angular, mottled and irregular surface treatment than 07. Similar small patches and bright contour interruptions recur across soft character forms, wood, stone and foliage. In the native hero crop the spectacles and wing boundary are less clean, while the blanket's weave is less orderly. In the workshop crop the table, canopy and surrounding vegetation gain busy faceted accents. The effect is visible in the full frame and at 1280/880, so it is not merely an extreme-magnification complaint. It makes the whole scene feel more uniformly processed and reduces the separation between the intended soft characters, supporting set and distant environment.

deductions.name: The workshop relationship remains more presented than exchanged
deductions.location: Center-left builder, toolbox and two stool guests
deductions.finding: The hammer, box and seated audience establish the activity. The builder's new tilt and low free mitten add friendliness, but the mitten does not clearly indicate a specific box detail, and the mostly frontal faces still read partly as a group presenting to the viewer. Dot's orientation helps. This is adequate as a warm park tableau, less precise as a captured moment of showing the guests how something works. It is not a reason to hide Clawd's accepted square eyes or invent finger-pointing.

deductions.name: Small-scale story becomes broad activity rather than interaction
deductions.weight: minor application ceiling; not a request to enlarge the cast
deductions.location: 420-wide local scale, particularly tree leaf and stool guests
deductions.finding: The foreground coder, tree moth and workshop still separate, but the tiny leaf exchange and exact watching relationship are difficult to resolve. The scene retains a coherent atmosphere and dominant moth; the specific secondary comedy cannot be treated as reliably communicated at that size.

criteriaForNine: Recover the cleaner material separation and stable contours demonstrated in 07 while preserving the chosen four-guest staging, current approved eye forms and tiny moth construction. Judge the entire image, not only repaired crops.

Keep background texture and isolated highlights subordinate enough that the three activity groups read before surface sparkle at 1280 and 880; preserve the open path and foreground lead at 420 without enlarging the cameos.

For a stronger story payoff, make the existing toolbox action and at least one guest's attention converge on the same visible feature through a small pose/contact cue. Preserve recognizable Clawd and simple mitten anatomy. This is a refinement criterion, not permission for a broad pose redesign.
A nine remains a judgment of an inspected result, not a promised score for agreeing to these criteria.

strengths: The large right-hand coding moth remains the unmistakable compositional lead. The bench, laptop, oversized head and glasses form one clear foreground mass; none of the four guests enters that scene.

The winding path supplies depth and breathing room between the foreground bench and left/middle activities. The tree arch and workshop canopy frame different spaces without dividing the panorama into panels. The lake and bridge extend the park beyond the cast.

The four cameos function as two small groups rather than four independent attractions. Muse and Grok share one leaf locally below the resting moth; Clawd and Dot have two readable stools beside the workshop. The requested parent-and-playing-children metaphor comes from spatial grouping, without aging or enlarging the moth.

The repeated moth remains recognizably the same oversized-head, compact-body character across coding, making and resting. Seated posture and normal occlusion do not require every wing to be displayed frontally. No new human-length limbs are needed for the scene.

Warm directional light, contact shadows, softened distant forms and blurred foreground foliage still provide a coherent dimensional foundation. The material regression is repairable within that established composition; it does not require a new park or more props.

Silent action is carried by visible objects and relationships: hand at keyboard, hammer with toolbox, stools facing a workshop area, resting pose and shared leaf. The image does not depend on dialogue, extra text or sound.
The enlarged companion crop shows dark Muse eyes and flat white Grok ovals without a visible internal pupil. That inspected correction is useful but does not settle the whole-frame quality judgment.

optional.name: Clarify the builder-to-toolbox invitation
optional.criterion: If one bounded acting refinement is retained, let the free mitten relate visibly to the near box edge while Dot attends. Keep Clawd's face and seated plush construction intact. This is secondary to recovering material clarity and should not justify another broad image reinterpretation.

optional.name: Keep the tree joke quiet
optional.criterion: The leaf group and resting silhouette already support the requested relationship. A tiny downward attention cue could sharpen it, but no larger reaction, new prop or adult-looking moth is warranted. Do not keep chasing micro-gaze at the cost of the whole image.

baselineComparison: 07 has the same strong park layout, guest count and foreground hierarchy. Its hero face and spectacle edges, blanket weave, bench boards and workshop forms read more cleanly as differentiated dimensional materials. 11 is brighter and more extensively patterned, with stronger scattered highlights and a changed builder tilt/free-hand pose. The current leaf contact and repaired companion eyes are specific useful details to preserve; they do not outweigh the broader clarity regression. This is a direct visual comparison, not a claim that every changed pixel or exact edit mechanism was audited. 07 is a control, not a wholesale replacement instruction.
